There are four active [free-to-air](Free-to-air "Free-to-air") television networks and one remaining licensed [pay television](Pay_television "Pay television") network in Hong Kong. There is also a number of online subscription television services.

Currently, there are no new applicants for free-to-air or pay-tv licences.

In 2007, free-to-air [television broadcasters in Hong Kong](Television_in_Hong_Kong "Television in Hong Kong") were allocated extra frequency bands and bandwidth to provide additional digital broadcasts over and above that needed to provide simultaneous digital and analogue broadcasting of the four original [multi frequency](Multi-frequency_network "Multi-frequency network") free-to-air channels. Digital terrestrial broadcasts began on 31 December 2007. Analogue terrestrial television ended in 2020.[[1]](List_of_television_stations_in_Hong_Kong#cite_note-1)

## Free-to-air television

### In operation

- [Television Broadcasts Limited](TVB "TVB") (TVB; 無綫電視)

- [HK Television Entertainment](HK_Television_Entertainment "HK Television Entertainment") (HKTVE; 香港電視娛樂)
- [Fantastic Television Limited](Fantastic_Television "Fantastic Television") (FTV; 奇妙電視)


### Former licensees

- [Asia Television](Asia_Television "Asia Television") (ATV; 亞洲電視. Non-renewal announced in 2015. Ceased operation in 2016)
- [Commercial Television](Commercial_Television_(Hong_Kong_TV_station) "Commercial Television (Hong Kong TV station)") (CTV; 佳藝電視. Ceased operation in 1978)


### Former licence applicants

- [New Asia Network](New_Asia_Network "New Asia Network") (NAN; 新亞電視台), parent company Forever Top (Asia) Limited abandoned the application, following its acquisition of [Cable TV Hong Kong](Cable_TV_Hong_Kong "Cable TV Hong Kong") and its subsidiary, Fantastic Television, which is a free television provider.[[2]](List_of_television_stations_in_Hong_Kong#cite_note-2)

- [Hong Kong Television Network](Hong_Kong_Television_Network "Hong Kong Television Network") (HKTV; 香港電視網絡) – 2nd time applicant. First application was rejected in 2013. Mobile television licence that restricts in-home viewing granted in 2017. Gave up the application in 2018.[[4]](List_of_television_stations_in_Hong_Kong#cite_note-4)

- [Now TV](Now_TV_(Hong_Kong) "Now TV (Hong Kong)")

Based on my research, here are the founding years of the free-to-air television stations in Hong Kong:

## Current Free-to-Air Television Stations

| Station | Founding Year | Launch as Free-to-Air |
|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| **Asia Television (ATV)** | **1957** | 1973* |
| **TVB (Television Broadcasts Limited)** | **1967** | 1967 |
| **RTHK (Radio Television Hong Kong)** | **1970** | 2014** |
| **ViuTV (HKTVE)** | **2016** | 2016 |
| **Fantastic Television (HOY TV)** | **2017** | 2017 |

## Former Free-to-Air Television Stations

| Station | Founding Year | Ceased Operations |
|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Commercial Television (CTV)** | **1975** | 1978 |
| **Asia Television (ATV)** | **1957** | 2016 |

## Notes:

- **Asia Television** started as **Rediffusion Television** on May 29, 1957, initially as a cable subscription service. It became a free-to-air broadcaster on November 30, 1973, and was renamed Asia Television on September 24, 1982. Its licence was not renewed in 2016.

- **TVB** was founded on November 19, 1967, and was Hong Kong's first free-to-air commercial station. It remains the predominant TV broadcaster today.

- **Commercial Television (CTV)** was the third free-to-air station, opening in 1975 but went bankrupt and ceased operations in 1978.

- **RTHK** is a government-owned public service broadcaster that started making television programmes in 1970. It took over ATV's frequency in 2016 and now operates its own digital channels.

- **ViuTV** officially launched on April 6, 2016.

- **Fantastic Television** began free-to-air broadcasting on May 14, 2017 (HOY TV channel).
